title: Autoinflammation triggered by aberrantly matured tRNAs (TRR237, Project A32N)
summary:
Certain rare inflammatory diseases have recently been linked to defects in a basic cellular process called tRNA maturation. tRNAs are small molecules that cells need to produce proteins correctly. Early findings from affected patients suggest that faulty tRNAs can inappropriately activate immune cells and trigger excessive inflammation.

In this study, we investigate how such defects lead to inflammatory responses in human immune cells. Our goal is to understand why the immune system mistakenly reacts to the body’s own molecules as if they were dangerous. In the long term, this research aims to improve our understanding of these diseases and support the development of better diagnostic and therapeutic approaches.
conditions: Patients with genetic defects in tRNA biology

interventions.name: Clinical autoinflammatory diseases caused by mutations in the tRNA machinery: Blood samples are collected from affected patients and healthy donors at the beginning of the study and at irregular intervals thereafter.
